title: Transactional Pulse — rough PRD & story bank
content:
Notes: sketching a compact feature to make per-transaction health and cost signals available to both clients (SDK/app) and our routing/runtime layers. Goal is to enable lightweight client-driven tradeoffs (e.g., high-fidelity vs budgeted responses) while preserving server-side safety and routing economics. Treat this as a small product experiment that can expand into policy controls for Dedicated/Private later.

Context / motivation:
- Customers building in-app assistants frequently want to: 1) surface a quick cost/latency estimate when a user composes a request; 2) optionally request a cheaper/shorter answer for low-value interactions; 3) observe request quality signals for debugging.
- Currently Redwood exposes per-token billing and per-request latency in logs/console, but there’s no compact signal surfaced at request time to inform client UX or automated fallbacks.
- We can reduce surprise and improve conversion if clients can show an estimated "Transaction Pulse" before sending or choose a fidelity preset that maps to runtime flavors.

Principles:
- Lightweight: minimal per-request overhead, backward-compatible with existing API surface.
- Declarative presets: clients pick from named fidelity buckets (e.g., quick, balanced, thorough) rather than tinkering with kernel-level knobs.
- Honest estimates: provide conservative token/latency ranges and a short reason code when estimates are degraded (e.g., cold-kv-cache, model-variant-fallback).
- Safe defaults: server may override client requests for SLO/security reasons; client must honor server-provided final routing decision.

Non-goals (for MVP):
- Full per-token forecasting or detailed cost breakdowns in the response.
- Per-customer revenue optimization or billing changes.
- Replacing Console metrics — this is a runtime/SDK feature, not a long-term analytics storage design.

User personas:
- Product PM / designer at a SaaS app: wants to show users an estimate and a cheap alternative for quick answers to reduce cost exposure.
- Platform engineer at a scale customer: wants to set a default fidelity for certain routes to control Dedicated spend.
- Developer integrating Redwood: wants a simple SDK hook and a deterministic server response when fidelity requests can’t be honored.

Key user stories (MVP):
1) As a frontend developer, I can request a named fidelity preset (quick | balanced | thorough) with my generation call, and receive an immediate estimate object indicating expected latency band and token range.
- Acceptance: SDK shows estimate within 200ms and server responds with {pulse_estimate} and final fidelity decision in same response.

2) As a product designer, I can surface a secondary CTA that says “faster (lower cost)” that maps to the quick preset; the dev can rely on the pulse estimate to decide whether to show the CTA.
- Acceptance: example UI spec plus example SDK sample implemented in playbook.

3) As an ops engineer, I can see in traces which requests requested a fidelity but were routed to a different variant (reason codes) so we can tune routing and capacity.
- Acceptance: trace includes pulse_request_fidelity and pulse_routing_reason fields.

4) As an integrator, if my preset cannot be honored (e.g., no compatible quantized variant available), the server returns the closest available preset and a reason string so client can gracefully notify user.
- Acceptance: server returns fallback_fidelity and fallback_reason.

API sketch (MVP):
- Client request additions (JSON on generation/chat endpoint):
  {
    "fidelity_preset": "quick" // optional: quick | balanced | thorough | custom
  }
- Server response additions (mvp):
  {
    "pulse": "estimate": "{\"latency_ms_min\":100, \"latency_ms_p50\":250, \"latency_ms_p90\":900}",
    "pulse": "decision": "{\"applied_fidelity\":\"balanced\", \"reason\":\"region_variants_unavailable\"}"
  }
- Implementation note: embed pulse fields in top-level response envelope to avoid breaking streaming starts; for streaming we emit a small header event with the pulse decision before tokens.

Runtime changes (high-level):
- Routing layer: evaluate client requested preset vs available model variants; pick nearest match and attach reason code (e.g., variant-mismatch, capacity-constrained, safety-lift).
- Estimator: lightweight profiler that uses sequence length heuristics, KV-cache hit prediction, recent latency percentiles for chosen model variant to produce conservative token/latency band.
- Telemetry: add pulse_request_fidelity, pulse_applied_fidelity, pulse_estimate_bands to traces/console (no long-term storage in MVP).

UX notes for SDKs and Console:
- JS SDK: accept fidelity_preset param; expose onEstimate callback and onDecision event. Provide small UI examples for toggling presets and showing estimated badge.
- Console: small per-route toggle to display pulse telemetry in traces; sample median estimate shown inline.

Metrics to evaluate success:
- Adoption: % of active API keys that set fidelity_preset at least once in 30 days.
- UX impact: conversion lift on CTA that surfaces cheaper preset (A/B test target +5% engagement reduction in cost per conversation).
- Accuracy: fraction of requests where actual latency/token counts fall within estimated p50/p90 bands (target 90% for p90 band conservative).

Risks / open questions:
- Will conservative estimates be too conservative and under-inform the UX? Need to tune profiler aggressively.
- Exposure: are we leaking too much internal routing detail via reason codes? Keep reason codes high-level and stable.
- Streaming implications: how to emit estimate before token stream starts in all SDKs? Need small header event emitted synchronously.

Next steps / short roadmap:
- Week 0-2: prototype estimator logic in serving-playground and wire a header event in JS SDK. Create mock UI example.
- Week 3-5: implement routing decision tagging + trace additions; run internal dogfood with 2-3 sandbox customers.
- Week 6-8: collect accuracy metrics, tighten estimator, draft developer docs and sample UI components.

Open todos (for me):
- Draft small header event format and ensure compatibility with streaming protocols.
- Confirm with privacy/security if reason codes need redaction for Private deployments.
- Build quick demo app that toggles fidelity and shows cost delta estimate (for sales/solutions).

Notes-to-self: keep API surface minimal and stable; prefer named presets over free-form knobs for now. This should be marketed internally as an "interaction guidance" feature rather than a billing control to avoid customer expectation mismatch.

End of sketch.
